_comment: What a foundation Korean course may never surface at random.
Two separate things live here, because they fail in two different ways.
`terms` is the word list. It exists because 보지 reached the Level Test as an
answer choice. The taught pack had already refused it — 004.jsonl carries the
entry with keep=0 and the reason written out — but the Level Test draws its
anchors from the *dictionary* as well, and there 보지 sits at level 4 glossed
'preservation', which is a real but obscure Sino-Korean noun. The spelling is
immediately read as a crude anatomical term by every Korean speaker alive, and
the gloss it was filed under is no defence at all.
`frames` is the part a word list cannot do. 여자 is a completely ordinary word
and 타다 is a completely ordinary verb, and 여자를 타요 is a sentence this
product must never generate. The harm is in the combination, so the check has
to run on the composed sentence and know that 여자 is a person and that 타다
takes a vehicle. See `content/vocabulary/noun-classes.json`.
This is an exclusion layer for RANDOM and GENERATED educational surfaces only.
The dictionary keeps its entries: a dictionary is allowed to contain adult
vocabulary and a learner who searches for it deliberately is not the risk. The
risk is a beginner meeting it in a four-choice question they did not ask for.
A predicate, and the noun classes that must never fill its object slot.
Each row is a real sentence the generators could produce. They are written as
the class rather than as the word so that adding 남자 or 아이 to the corpus
cannot reopen a hole that closing 여자 shut.

rules.why: 여자를 타요 — 타다 takes a vehicle, and with a person it is sexual.
동생을 드세요 — eating a person or a body part.
여자를 만져요 — non-consensual or sexual reading.
아이를 때려요 — violence against a person or animal.
빈 몸을 버렸어요 — disposing of a person or a body part.

_comment: Tier one: never anywhere a learner can reach without asking for it.
Matched against the whole headword, not as a substring, so 년도 and 청소년
are untouched by the entry for 년 below — which is in the other tier anyway.
The dictionary keeps these; only the teaching and generating surfaces refuse.
Tier two: legitimately taught, and never usable as a bare option.
년 is taught as the counter for years and its example is 이 년 동안
배웠어요, which is correct and useful. Standing alone in a list of four it
is read as the insult, and it stood alone in 년이 요리를 해요. 새끼 is the
same shape: taught as a young animal with 고양이 새끼가 귀여워요, and on its
own it is one of the strongest things you can call somebody.
The rest are bound nouns — 명, 살, 원 never appear without a number in front
of them, so as a standalone answer choice they are not words a learner has
ever met.

질, 사정 and 기생 were on the excluded list and are off it: each is an everyday word — quality, circumstances, a parasite — and an exact-match exclusion would have taken the everyday sense with the other one. 벌, 개, 잔, 번 and 원 came off the bound-noun list for the same reason: the curriculum teaches them as a bee, a dog, a drinking glass, a time and the won, and they are perfectly good answer choices.
